annotation.title_clean: Правовые аспекты гражданско-правовой ответственности за причинение вреда действиями робота как квазисубъекта гражданско-правовых отношений
annotation.title_en: Legal Aspects of Civil Liability for Damages in Tort Caused by the Actions of a Robot as a Quasi-Subject of Civil Law Relations
annotation.venue: Гуманитарная информатика (Humanitarian Informatics), Tomsk State University
named_instruments_referenced: Civil Code of the Russian Federation
annotation.summary_en: This Russian legal-doctrinal article looks at tort liability for harm caused by autonomous AI robots, such as self-driving cars and industrial robots. It proposes treating the robot as a quasi-subject of civil law and adding a special tort to the Russian Civil Code. It also proposes a classifier that sorts cases by tort category, level of damage, the responsible person and the industry involved.
key_provisions_or_claims: Robots fall into two groups: autonomous robots with AI ('Robots') and simple programmable machines without AI.
An autonomous Robot cannot be treated as a source of increased danger or as a defective product under current Russian law.
Responsible persons can include the inventor, the programmer, the manufacturer, the owner/user and a third party.
The authors propose a classifier of tort categories (A–C), damage levels, responsible-person categories (I–IV) and an industry code, which they say could cut court costs.
The Civil Code should be amended to introduce the Robot as a quasi-subject of civil law relations.
